trial_title: POPQ Associated With Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy
brief_summary: The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the impact of different hysterectomy (removal of the uterus) techniques on the risk of pelvic organ prolapse (situation when one or more of your pelvic organs like your bladder, uterus, or rectum have dropped down or slipped out of their normal position, sometimes even bulging into the vagina) and urinary incontinence (leaking urine unexpectedly) in women aged 18-85 who underwent hysterectomy or supracervical hysterectomy (removing of the uteru

eligibility_table.criterion: persons who underwent total or subtotal hysterectomy for benign conditions regardless of the type of surgery
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not undergone a hysterectomy, so this criterion is not applicable.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone a total or subtotal hysterectomy for benign conditions within the last 12 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: agree to participate and to follow-up
eligibility_table.justification: The patient can agree to participate and follow-up as there are no indications of refusal.

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a confirmed diagnosis of a viable intrauterine pregnancy based on transvaginal ultrasound findings?
Does the patient have an ECOG performance status score of >2?

eligibility_table.criterion: pelvic organ prolapse prior to the surgery
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about pelvic organ prolapse, making it unclear if this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a pelvic organ prolapse classified as stage II or higher according to the POP-Q system?

eligibility_table.criterion: surgery due to malignant conditions (ovarian, cervical or endometrial cancer)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's history does not indicate surgery due to malignant conditions, but there is no definitive information to confirm this.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a confirmed diagnosis of ovarian, cervical, or endometrial cancer based on histopathological examination?
